notes: Changed the board type from step 1: arduino-mkr1000 has no digital pin ports (only USB, VIN, VCC, GND, BAT), so pin 2 cannot be wired. I used arduino-mkr1000-wifi, which has D2 and GND. Its catalogue name says MKR WiFi 1010, but its id matches the tutorial's store link (arduino-mkr1000-wifi). The circuit image shows an MKR1000, so this is a catalogue approximation.
Parts are unchanged from step 1: board, breadboard, LED, 82 ohm resistor, and two jumper wires.
The resistor is 82 ohm per the parts list. The schematic label says 220 ohm.

Layout read from the image: green wire from pin 2 to column 3. Resistor from column 3 to column 6. LED anode in column 6 (resistor side) and cathode in column 8. Black wire from column 8 to GND. I used the upper block of the breadboard image as bank 't', rows a-e.
Current path: D2, then resistor, then LED anode, then LED cathode, then GND. This matches the schematic.
